thread:
maria: quick idea — after last night's paging mess, i sketched a tiny proposal for improving our post-incident follow-ups. can we discuss?

*simon: yes please — eager to hear. the handoff confusion was the main pain point for me.*

maria: tl;dr: build a lightweight 'action-queue' that the incident bot creates automatically when an incident is marked resolved. it would: auto-schedule a postmortem within 72h, create action items with owners and due dates, push to a simple dashboard, and remind owners twice before due.

jess: love that. so it’s like a bridge between incident timeline -> postmortem -> tracked actions. would the bot open tickets somewhere or just keep them in a dashboard?

maria: optionally both. default flow = create dashboard entries + create tickets in our internal tracker only if owner opts in (to avoid noise). bot message would look like: 

```
postmortem-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 resolved. Postmortem scheduled: Thu 2026-04-02 10:00 UTC.
Action items: 3 (assign with `/pm assign <id> @owner`)
See: <link-to-actionboard/INC-2026-345>
```

kevin: small nit — make sure the bot captures customer impact classification (none/partial/major) and any committed customer communications so follow-ups aren't forgotten. that was missed last time.

maria: agreed. propose adding structured tags: severity, customer_impact, sla_breach(boolean), customer_contacts. bots can prefill by scraping incident metadata.

simon: on the scheduling bit — who gets invited to the postmortem? historically it's the oncall + owners + product + eng leads. bot should suggest attendees based on who touched the runbook and who had alerts. also include a 'deputy' field for handoffs so oncall can flag a replacement if needed.

jess: example flow for an incident: 
1) incident resolved -> bot creates action-queue (entries + suggested owners)
2) bot posts in channel with quick buttons: Schedule PM, Edit attendees, Create tickets, Acknowledge
3) first ack within 24h confirms PM scheduled, otherwise auto-schedule provisional slot

maria: and we should surface high-risk items (e.g., customer-facing regression) as high-priority in the queue so they bubble to top of dashboard.

postmortem-bot: (bot suggestion) add a default template for action items: 
- title: string
- owner: @handle
- due: ISO date
- impact: low/medium/high
- notes: one-line
- linked incident: INC-id

kevin: can the bot do periodic audits? e.g., weekly report of overdue actions + stale PMs older than 30d? would help SRE manager follow up.

maria: yes — scheduled audit report + optional slack reminders to owners. also add a single command for oncall to escalate overdue actions: `/pm escalate <action-id> @manager`. The bot should attach last contact log.

simon: what about integrating with our calendar and timezone handling? last PM had a lot of timezone back-and-forth. bot should propose slots using free/busy for attendees, or suggest async writeups if no common slot within 72h.

jess: i'd like a small prototype first — minimal viable features: auto-create action-queue, post message with buttons, and dashboard view. no ticket integration initially. we can iterate.

maria: volunteer list? i can mock the bot message and dashboard UI. simon, can you do scheduling logic? kevin, can you add the audit/report bits after MVP? jess, you coordinate UX + write the PM template.

simon: yep — i'll take scheduling.

kevin: ok for audit/report later.

jess: happy to do template + coordination.

maria: goal: ship MVP behind a feature flag in two sprints. run it on eng-oncall for a trial. if it helps, roll to incidents channel.

oncall-bot: reminder — please add the incident ID when you create a manual postmortem. use `/pm new INC-2026-345` to prefill fields.

maria: next steps: i'll drop a one-pager with the proposed bot messages, dashboard wireframe, and the PM template. want feedback by EOD Friday. if no objections, we'll add an RFC to eng-runtime backlog.

simon: sounds good. quick question — do we want the bot to auto-assign owners based on last editor of the runbook step? that could help but might be inaccurate.

maria: make auto-assignment opt-in and visibly suggested, not forced. keep human in the loop.

jess: also let's include a little audit log per action: created_by, last_pinged, status changes. makes follow-up easier for managers.

maria: perfect. thanks team. i'll ping the thread when the one-pager is up.

kevin: thanks — big quality-of-life win if we get this right.

postmortem-bot: (system) Incident INC-2026-345 — summary: brief outage of inference runtime (cache eviction bug). Resolved at 2026-03-28T03:14:22Z. Customer impact: partial degradation for 12 minutes. See: internal/INC-2026-345/summary

maria: noted — i'll include that incident as the first trial case in the doc.

jess: +1. excited to see the mockups.

simon: thanks, marking action: schedule proto planning meeting (maria, simon, jess, kevin) — proposed Thu 2026-04-09 15:00 UTC.

maria: added.

oncall-bot: (reminder) if you are taking an oncall handoff, run `/handoff start @new_oncall` to transfer the incident context card.

maria: noted. done.

jess: ok that's it from me for now. will review the one-pager when posted.

maria: thanks all — closing thread for now, will reopen when doc is up.
